messages.author: cdb8abc160f16f50
messages.subject: Another question regarding yearly-site covariates
parts:
Hello:
I just realized that colonization and extinction is estimated for a year less than the total number of years that the data was collected.  In other words, the yearly-site covariates would have five years of data, but the colonization can only be measured for four years. Using the same example as before, I have 5 years of coyote relative abundance site-year data. I'm wondering how dynamic occupancy is using five years of relative abundance for coyotes to calculate its impact on four years of bobcat colonization.
Best,
Xinzhu

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Another question regarding yearly-site covariates
parts:
Dear Xinzhu,

yes, it matters, since with 5 years, a site-year covariate must have 5 columns, even if only 4 of them are used for colonization and extinction.

BUT: this covariate may also be used for detection, and there we need 5 columns. So, this solution has apparently saved the unmarked developers to create two types of such covariates, one for the dynamics params and another one for p.

Best regards  --- Marc
